#!/bin/bash

# Script to count lines containing a specified file extension
# Usage: ./count_lines.sh <extension> [filename]
# The extension should be like ".txt"
# The filename defaults to the first .txt file in the directory if not specified

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

EXTENSION="${1:-.txt}"

if [ -z "$2" ]; then
    # Find the first text file in the directory
    FILENAME=$(ls *.txt 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
    if [ -z "$FILENAME" ]; then
        FILENAME=$(ls | head -n 1)
    fi
else
    FILENAME="$2"
fi

if [ -z "$FILENAME" ]; then
    echo "No file found in the directory"
    exit 1
fi

# Count lines containing the specified extension
COUNT=$(grep -c "$EXTENSION" "$FILENAME")

echo "$COUNT"
EOF
chmod +x files_list/count_lines.sh
